title: T-Cell Engagers Targeting BCMA, GPRC5D, or FcRH5 in Relapsed/ Refractory Multiple Myeloma, Landscape Beyond CAR-T Cell Therapy, a Systematic Review and Network Meta Analysis
content:
Background:

Relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) is marked by frequent triple-class refractoriness and poor survival, whereas bispecific antibodies targeting BCMA, GPRC5D, or FcRH5 show meaningful activity even in heavily pretreated populations. This meta-analysis evaluates and compares the efficacy and safety of these agents in RRMM.

Methods: We searched 7 databases and finalised 44 studies.

Results: Versus SOC, odds of ORR were higher with Talquetamab, Teclistamab, Elranatamab, and Linvoseltamab (5.73, 4.86, 3.84, 2.63). PFS improved with Teclistamab (0.50, 0.36-0.55), Talquetamab (0.50, 0.36-0.55), Elranatamab (0.45, 0.36-0.55), and Linvoseltamab (0.23, 0.17-0.31). OS was longer with Linvoseltamab (0.41, 0.24-0.70) and Elranatamab (0.58, 0.43-0.78), but shorter with Teclistamab (1.82, 1.37-2.42) and Talquetamab (1.75, 1.20-2.57). In pooled single-arm data, Talquetamab had the highest ORR (72%) and CRS (68%); Teclistamab and Linvoseltamab showed ORR 61% with CRS 51%. Cevostamab and Elranatamab had ORR 49% and 56% with CRS 61% and 52% respectively.

Conclusion: In RRMM, all bispecific antibodies improved ORR and PFS as compared to SOC. Linvoseltamab/Elranatamab improved OS, Talquetamab/Teclistamab worsened OS versus SOC.
